INTEGRATIVE, COMPARATIVE AND MARINE BIOLOGY, PH.D.
Graduate Coordinator: Dr. Amanda Williard
The Department of Biology and Marine Biology offers a program of study and research leading to the Doctor of Philosophy in Integrative, Comparative and Marine Biology. The program provides students with a background in targeted areas of biology and marine biology based on the diverse interests of the faculty within the department. As is generally the case, the Ph.D. program is primarily a research degree. As such, it is intended to serve students with interests in conducting research in academia, industry, and government along with those who intend to become faculty in undergraduate teaching institutions, managers in technology-based industries and policy makers in government. Students will learn the process of identifying, defining and addressing an original research question. The program also includes a teaching practicum with classroom instruction in pedagogical techniques and technologies along with lecture experience under the guidance of a faculty mentor.
Admission requirements
Students will be admitted to the Ph.D. program by a majority vote of the Graduate Advisory Committee (GAC) and with the support of a faculty advisor in the Department of Biology and Marine Biology. Under most circumstances, students admitted to the program will have:
A bachelor’s degree in biology or a related discipline from an accredited U.S. college or university or its equivalent at an international institution based on a four-year program.
An overall grade point average of at least 3.0 out of 4.0.
A record of research, applied learning or relevant professional experience.
Applicants seeking admission to the doctoral program in biology should contact prospective faculty advisors and are required to submit the following to the Graduate School:
An application for graduate admission
Transcripts of all college work (undergraduate and graduate)
Three recommendation letters by individuals in professionally relevant fields
Curriculum vitae Statement of Interest for Ph.D. research, including a summary of relevant experience (maximum of three pages)
Copies of any publications (if applicable)
Application and supporting documents must be submitted by the published deadline.
NOTE: The Graduate Record of Examination (GRE) General Test is not required for admission. Academic record, relevant work experience, research experience, and recommendations are used in concert to determine acceptability. The applicant must secure a position in a faculty advisor’s research group in order to be admitted into the program.
Degree Requirements (60 post-baccalaureate credit hours)
The program requires 60 post-baccalaureate credit hours of graduate study. A minimum of 24 credit hours of graduate study must be completed in residence.
The maximum amount of credit that a Ph.D. student may count toward a doctorate from a master’s degree program is 30 credit hours. This applies whether the master’s degree was earned at UNCW or elsewhere. Six post-M.S. credit hours of credit may be transferred from another accredited institution. Grades earned on transfer work must be equivalent to “B” or better and must be approved by the Graduate Advisory Committee.
Dissertation Research: The student must present a prospectus outlining their dissertation research plan prior to the beginning of the third year in the Ph.D. program.
Each student must pass a Candidacy Exam that includes an oral examination based on the student’s dissertation prospectus. The Candidacy Exam should be taken before the beginning of the third year in the Ph.D. program.
The student must complete and defend a dissertation based on a research program approved by the student’s dissertation committee that results in an original, high quality, significant, and substantial body of research. The student must present their dissertation in a public seminar and successfully complete an oral defense of the dissertation prior to graduation.
All requirements for the degree must be completed within six years after admission to the Ph.D. program.
Required Courses
Core Courses
BIO 501 - Introduction to Science as a Profession Credit Hours: 2 (2 credits required)
BIO 690 - Biology Seminar Credit Hours: 2
BIO 694 - Practicum in College Biology Teaching Credit Hours: 2
BIO 699 - Dissertation Credit Hours: 1 To 12
In addition to the above requirements, students must consult with their thesis advisory committee to select two additional courses that complement their thesis research and satisfy individual needs and interests. Select two of the following courses:
BIO 519 - Advanced Topics in Cellular and Molecular Biology Credit Hours: 3
BIO 534 - Advanced Topics in Ecology and Evolution Credit Hours: 3
BIO 549 - Advanced Topics in Physiology and Biochemistry Credit Hours: 3
BIO 564 - Advanced Topics in Marine Biology and Oceanography Credit Hours: 3
Elective Courses
All elective credit (minimum of 36 credit hours) to be selected from BIO and BIOL courses numbered 500-699. Graduate courses from other disciplines may also be selected, with approval of the student’s thesis committee.
Exit Requirements
Each student must pass a Candidacy Exam that includes an oral examination based on the student’s dissertation prospectus. The Candidacy Exam should be taken before the beginning of the third year in the Ph.D. program.
The student must complete and defend a dissertation based on a research program approved by the student’s dissertation committee that results in an original, high quality, significant, and substantial body of research. The student must present their dissertation in a public seminar and successfully complete an oral defense of the dissertation prior to graduation.
